1: Surah Al-Fatiha (Chapter 1 of the Holy Quran), "The Opening", is recited in every unit of every prayer. The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) called it the greatest surah in the Quran and "the seven oft-repeated verses" (Sahih al-Bukhari).
2: Surah Al-Baqarah (Chapter 2 of the Holy Quran) is the longest surah of the Quran, covering faith, worship, law and lessons from earlier nations. The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) said that Shaytan flees from a house in which Surah Al-Baqarah is recited (Sahih Muslim).
2:255: Ayat al-Kursi (Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 255) describes the majesty, knowledge and eternal power of Allah. The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) said it is the greatest verse in the Book of Allah (Sahih Muslim).
2:285-286: The last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah are a declaration of faith and a beautiful supplication. The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) said: whoever recites these two verses at night, they will be sufficient for him (Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim).
12: Surah Yusuf (Chapter 12 of the Holy Quran) tells the complete story of Prophet Yusuf (AS) — his patience, trust in Allah and forgiveness. Allah Himself calls it "the best of stories" (Quran 12:3).
18: Surah Al-Kahf (Chapter 18 of the Holy Quran) contains the stories of the People of the Cave, Musa (AS) and Al-Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn — lessons on faith, knowledge, wealth and power. The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) said that whoever memorises the first ten verses of Surah Al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal (Sahih Muslim).
19: Surah Maryam (Chapter 19 of the Holy Quran) is named after Maryam (AS), the mother of Isa (AS). It recounts the stories of Zakariya, Yahya, Maryam, Isa and Ibrahim (peace be upon them all) and the mercy of Allah.
36: Surah Ya-Sin (Chapter 36 of the Holy Quran) affirms the message of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), reflects on the signs of Allah in creation, and reminds us of the reality of resurrection and the Hereafter.
55: Surah Ar-Rahman (Chapter 55 of the Holy Quran), "The Most Merciful", lists the countless blessings of Allah and asks 31 times: "Which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?"
56: Surah Al-Waqi'ah (Chapter 56 of the Holy Quran), "The Inevitable Event", describes the Day of Judgement and the three groups of people on that Day: the foremost, the companions of the right, and the companions of the left.
67: Surah Al-Mulk (Chapter 67 of the Holy Quran) reminds us that all sovereignty belongs to Allah. The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) said that a surah of thirty verses interceded for a man until he was forgiven — Tabarak alladhi biyadihil-mulk (Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi, graded hasan).
97: Surah Al-Qadr (Chapter 97 of the Holy Quran) speaks of Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Decree, in which the Quran was revealed — a night better than a thousand months.
103: Surah Al-Asr (Chapter 103 of the Holy Quran) teaches in three verses that all of mankind is in loss, except those who believe, do righteous deeds, and advise one another to truth and patience.
108: Surah Al-Kawthar (Chapter 108 of the Holy Quran) is the shortest surah of the Quran. It tells of Al-Kawthar, the river in Paradise granted by Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) (Sahih Muslim).
112: Surah Al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112 of the Holy Quran) explains the pure concept of Tawheed (the Oneness of Allah). The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) said that reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas is equivalent to reciting one-third of the Quran (Sahih al-Bukhari).
113: Surah Al-Falaq (Chapter 113 of the Holy Quran) teaches us to seek refuge in Allah from the evil of His creation, the darkness of night, sorcery and envy. The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) recited it with Al-Ikhlas and An-Nas every night before sleeping (Sahih al-Bukhari).
114: Surah An-Nas (Chapter 114 of the Holy Quran), the final surah of the Quran, teaches us to seek refuge in Allah, the Lord, King and God of mankind, from the whispers of Shaytan. The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) recited it with Al-Ikhlas and Al-Falaq every night before sleeping (Sahih al-Bukhari).
